meta.subtitle: Fiscal 2026: AI infrastructure orders lift growth, but memory costs and a full multiple keep the call at HOLD

advisories: model vs Street expected return diverge by 85pp — informational, not scored

analystSentiment.commentary:
Cisco closed fiscal 2026 with revenue of $63.3B, up 12% on the company's figures, and GAAP diluted EPS of $3.33, up 31%. The growth came from product, especially Networking, while services revenue was flat and subscription revenue grew 1%. That mix matters: the company says product gross margin fell on product mix and higher memory costs, and on a non-GAAP basis Q4 fiscal 2026 gross margin was 66.3% against 68.4% a year earlier.

The demand evidence is strong. The August 12, 2026 earnings release reports Q4 product orders up 35% year over year (up 25% excluding hyperscalers), AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers of $9.3 billion for fiscal 2026, and an expected $7.5 billion of AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers in fiscal 2027. Management guides fiscal 2027 revenue to $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion.

The price already reflects much of this. At $112.82 the stock trades at 21.9x consensus FY27E EPS of $5.15, which sits above the top of the company's non-GAAP guidance, and at 33.9x trailing GAAP earnings. Our probability-weighted value sits modestly above the price but short of the BUY threshold, and the bear case, a pause in hyperscaler spending combined with further margin pressure, is a plausible outcome rather than a tail. We rate CSCO HOLD with a 12-month target range of $105 to $140.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Cisco Systems designs and sells networking, security, collaboration and observability technology, plus the services that support it, to businesses, public institutions, governments and service providers. It sells directly and through systems integrators, service providers, resellers and distributors, and was incorporated in 1984.

The company reports as a single reportable segment. Fiscal 2026 revenue was $63.3B, of which product revenue rose 16% and services revenue was flat. The 10-K says it is incorporating AI into its portfolios and integrating its products more tightly into a platform.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: Cisco's growth has turned up on hyperscaler AI infrastructure and campus networking demand, and the fiscal 2027 guidance implies further acceleration. Against that, the growth is hardware-led, product gross margin is under pressure from mix and memory costs, and free cash flow fell in fiscal 2026 while inventories rose. The stock trades at 21.9x consensus FY27E EPS, a non-GAAP basis, which leaves limited room if hyperscaler orders slow. The weighted outcome sits a little above the price, so we rate HOLD rather than chase the Street's Buy consensus.

catalysts: Delivery of the $7.5 billion of hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue the company expects in fiscal 2027; see Growth.
Q1 fiscal 2027 results against guidance of $18.0 billion to $18.2 billion of revenue and non-GAAP EPS of $1.32 to $1.34.
Non-GAAP gross margin holding inside the guided 65% - 66% range for Q1 fiscal 2027 despite memory costs; see Financials.
Order growth outside hyperscalers, which the release puts at 25% in Q4 fiscal 2026; see Growth.
risks: Customer concentration in hyperscaler AI demand, about 6% of fiscal 2026 revenue; see Risks.
Memory constraints and costs squeezing product gross margin; see Risks.
Inventory and purchase-commitment exposure if demand slows; see Risks.
A forward multiple that already discounts the guided growth; see Valuation.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended Late July (FY26 ended July 25, 2026).

financials.incomeCommentary:
Fiscal 2026 revenue rose to $63.3B, up 12% on the company's figures (the vendor table shows +11.8%), after +5.3% in FY25 and -5.6% in FY24. The company attributes the increase to product revenue, up 16%, while services were flat; total software revenue was $23.2 billion, up 4%, and subscription revenue rose 1%. For Q4 fiscal 2026 the company reports revenue up 18% year over year to $17.3 billion; the vendor snapshot shows +16%, and we use the company's figure.

Gross margin slipped to 64.5% from 64.9%. The company explains the {- 0.5 percentage point -} decline in product gross margin by product mix and higher memory costs, partly offset by productivity, pricing actions, lower intangibles amortization and the absence of a fiscal 2025 supplier-dispute charge. On a non-GAAP basis the pressure is clearer: Q4 non-GAAP product gross margin was 64.8% against 67.5% a year earlier.

Operating leverage did the work. Research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses fell by {+ 3.4 percentage points +} of revenue, and operating margin rose to 24.3% from 20.8%. The company attributes the 31% rise in diluted EPS to revenue growth and operating margin improvement. Below the operating line, other income swung from a small loss in fiscal 2025 to a gain in fiscal 2026, and the excerpt does not explain the swing, while the effective tax rate rose to 17.1% from 8.3%.

GAAP and non-GAAP earnings diverge widely. Fiscal 2026 non-GAAP EPS was $4.33 against GAAP EPS of $3.33, and the gap persists in fiscal 2027 guidance (GAAP $4.00 to $4.06, non-GAAP $5.05 to $5.11). Restructuring and other charges were $693 million for the year. The income statement is healthier than a year ago, but its improvement rests on hardware volume rather than margin.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended Late July (FY26 ended July 25, 2026).

financials.balanceCommentary:
Total debt was $29.5B at fiscal year-end, including commercial paper, up from $28.1B. Short-term debt rose to $10,161 million from $5,232 million, so a larger share of borrowings now falls due within a year. The vendor's net debt of $22.3B is total debt minus cash and cash equivalents only; we use that basis. The company reports cash and cash equivalents and investments of $15.9 billion, which would leave a smaller net figure if investments were counted, while the vendor's cash and short-term investments line shows $14.3B; the two differ in what they include.

Inventories rose to $5,694 million from $3,164 million. The 10-K excerpt does not explain the rise, though its risk factors note that managing component supply challenges has in the past increased inventory and purchase commitments. The provision for inventory and purchase commitments fell to $387 million from $493 million, so the build has not yet produced write-downs.

The current ratio is 0.93, below 1.00 in FY25, and interest coverage on trailing figures is 10.5x. Equity rose to $50.3B. The balance sheet is serviceable, but the inventory build and heavier short-term maturities make it less flexible than a year ago.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended Late July (FY26 ended July 25, 2026).

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Operating cash flow was $14.2 billion in fiscal 2026, flat on fiscal 2025, even as net income rose 30%. Capital expenditure increased to $1.4B from $0.9B, so free cash flow fell to $12.8B from $13.3B and FCF margin fell to 20.2% from 23.5%. Earnings growth has therefore not yet reached cash, and working capital, including the inventory build covered under the balance sheet, is the likely place it went, although the excerpt does not break it down.

Share repurchases of $6.1B and dividends of $6.6B together absorbed nearly all of fiscal 2026 free cash flow. That pace leaves little internal funding for acquisitions or debt reduction without slowing buybacks. The trailing FCF yield of 2.9% is thin for a company of this maturity and is the main reason we do not treat the cash return as a valuation floor.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On trailing GAAP earnings CSCO trades at 33.9x, with EV/EBITDA of 24.7x and P/S of 7.0x. The vendor's forward P/E of 21.9x labelled NTM matches the price over consensus FY27E EPS of $5.15, so it is effectively a current-fiscal-year multiple; on FY28E EPS of $5.62 the forward P/E is ~20.1x. Both forward figures rest on consensus estimates that sit above the top of the company's non-GAAP FY27 guidance, so they are non-GAAP multiples, not GAAP ones.

We do not use peer multiples. The vendor's peer set mixes networking with unrelated businesses, and no comparable peer figures are available here. Against its own history, the trailing GAAP multiple is high because fiscal 2026 GAAP EPS still carries amortization and restructuring that the non-GAAP figures exclude. The forward multiple is reasonable for revenue growth the company guides into the mid-teens, but it is not cheap for a business whose services revenue is flat and whose free cash flow fell.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Hyperscaler AI orders keep compounding, fiscal 2027 lands at or above the top of guidance, and non-GAAP gross margin holds near Q4 levels. The market pays a multiple in the mid-to-high twenties on FY28E EPS of $5.62, still below the Street high target of $170.00.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Cisco meets fiscal 2027 guidance and the FY28E consensus EPS used in Bull holds. Today's 21.9x forward multiple rolls onto that FY28E figure over 12 months, a value below the consensus target of $136.16.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Hyperscaler orders pause and memory costs push margins lower, so earnings land at the low end of FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance, $5.05, and the multiple compresses to the high teens as growth fades.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
We value CSCO over a 12-month horizon on non-GAAP EPS, because that is the basis of consensus and of the forward multiples; GAAP EPS is lower, as covered under Financials. Base at $123 is the simplest checkable case: today's forward multiple on FY27E rolls forward onto FY28E consensus EPS. Bull at $150 needs both upside to guidance and a higher multiple. Bear at $90 pairs the bottom of the FY27 guidance range with a high-teens multiple; the 52-week low of $66.81 shows the stock has traded well below that within the year, and the Street low target of $110.00 is too close to the price to serve as a real downside.

We weight Bull and Bear equally at 25% each, with 50% on Base. The case for more Bull weight is real: Q4 orders, the hyperscaler order backlog and a fiscal 2027 guide calling for faster growth. The case against is equally concrete: the growth is concentrated in hyperscaler AI infrastructure, non-GAAP gross margin fell year over year in Q4, free cash flow declined, and the stock has already risen from its 52-week low toward the $130.37 high. The sources do not explain the price path, but it means much of the order momentum is in the price.

The call is reasonably close. Shifting five points of weight from Bear to Bull would lift the expected return to around the BUY threshold with reward/risk near its floor, which is the kind of narrow BUY the desk has seen fail in review. We do not think that shift is justified until margins show they can hold through the memory cycle, so the derived label is HOLD.

The target range of $105 to $140 brackets Base and spans moderate downside to a value near the Street consensus.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Cisco reports a single reportable segment, so all of fiscal 2026 revenue of $63.3B sits here. Product revenue grew 16% for the year, led by Networking at 22%, which the company ties particularly to AI Infrastructure and Campus Networking. Security product revenue grew 2% for the year but 14% in Q4 fiscal 2026, Collaboration 4% and Observability 4%. Services revenue was flat. The mix is moving toward hardware, since software and subscription revenue grew more slowly than product, as covered under Financials. That raises growth now but lowers the share of revenue that recurs.

moatFactors.name: Installed base and services attach
moatFactors.body: Remaining performance obligations were $46.7 billion at fiscal year-end, up 7%, and deferred revenue was $29.8 billion, up 3%. Contracted revenue of that size gives visibility and reflects a large installed base that buys support and renewals. The counter-point is that services revenue was flat in fiscal 2026, so the base is stable rather than expanding.

moatFactors.name: Networking scale and breadth
moatFactors.body: Cisco sells across campus, data center, wireless, service-provider and hyperscaler networks, and the release reports Networking product orders up 40% in Q4 fiscal 2026, an eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. Breadth lets it bundle security and observability into the platform. The risk factors note that price and product competition can change rapidly with technological innovation, so scale does not guarantee share in new AI architectures.

moatFactors.name: Pricing power
moatFactors.body: The company credits pricing actions with partly offsetting margin pressure, which shows some ability to pass on costs. Yet product gross margin still fell on mix and memory costs, and non-GAAP gross margin fell in Q4. Pricing protects margins at the edges rather than insulating them.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. The installed base, the contracted backlog and the breadth of the networking portfolio are durable advantages, and they let Cisco participate in hyperscaler AI build-outs without being a newcomer. The moat is narrower than the revenue scale suggests because the revenue driving growth is hardware sold to a concentrated set of hyperscalers, where the risk factors describe rapid price and technology competition, and because recurring revenue lines grew slowly in fiscal 2026. A widening would show up as subscription and services growth catching up with product growth; a narrowing as gross margin erosion that pricing cannot offset.

points: Hyperscaler AI infrastructure is the main driver. The August 12, 2026 release reports $9.3 billion of such orders in fiscal 2026, including $4 billion in Q4, approximately $4 billion of related revenue in fiscal 2026 and $7.5 billion expected in fiscal 2027. The 10-K puts hyperscalers at approximately 6% of fiscal 2026 revenue, up from less than 2% in fiscal 2025, and the company expects this demand to remain a significant driver in fiscal 2027.

Demand is broadening beyond hyperscalers. Q4 fiscal 2026 product orders rose 35% year over year and 25% excluding hyperscalers, with double-digit growth across every geography and customer market per the release. Orders lead revenue, so this supports the near-term guide; it does not show how durable the cycle is.

Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue of $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion, consistent with consensus FY27E revenue of ~$73.2B (+16%). Consensus then expects FY28E revenue of $78.1B, a marked slowdown from the fiscal 2027 pace, which tells us the Street already treats part of fiscal 2027 as a cyclical peak.

Software and security are the slower legs, as the fiscal 2026 product mix shows. In Q4 the company closed two acquisitions, Galileo Technologies (observability) and Astrix Securities (Non-Human Identity security); the release does not disclose their size, so their contribution to growth cannot yet be judged.

The main constraint on growth is supply and cost. The 10-K cites a highly competitive and complex environment, especially memory constraints and costs and trade policy, so component availability could cap how much of the order book converts on schedule.

management.leadership: Chuck Robbins is Chair and CEO, and Mark Patterson is CFO, per the August 12, 2026 earnings release. The fiscal 2025 proxy (filed 2025-10-28) lists R. Scott Herren as former Executive Vice President and CFO, and names Jeetendra (Jeetu) Patel as President and Chief Product Officer. Management's stated focus for fiscal 2027 is durable growth, consistent profitability and continued capital returns while investing in growth opportunities. Execution in fiscal 2026 was good: the release says Q4 revenue, non-GAAP operating income and EPS all exceeded the high end of guidance. The test now is margin management through the memory cycle rather than demand generation.
management.capitalAllocation: Cisco returns most of its free cash flow. In Q4 fiscal 2026 it returned $3.2 billion through buybacks and dividends, repurchasing approximately 13 million shares at an average price of $111.53, close to today's price. The remaining repurchase authorization is $8.1 billion with no termination date, and the board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.42 per share, payable October 21, 2026; future dividends remain subject to board approval. Buybacks at prices near the current level look reasonable against our Base value but not compelling. With free cash flow down and short-term debt up, we would prefer the company not lean on borrowing to sustain the return pace.
management.governance: Per the fiscal 2025 proxy filed 2025-10-28, all directors other than Mr. Robbins are independent, all members of the Audit, Compensation and Nomination and Governance Committees are independent, and Mr. Capellas serves as Lead Independent Director while Mr. Robbins combines the Chair and CEO roles. The combined role concentrates authority, which the board offsets with a lead independent director who chairs executive sessions. Say-on-pay support was approximately 77% at the prior meeting, up from approximately 75%. That is passing but soft support, and the proxy says the company engaged holders of approximately 61% of shares partly in response. We view governance as adequate, with pay alignment the item to monitor.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy excerpt available here carries no beneficial-ownership table, so we cannot assess insider stakes. No holder is identified as having a controlling position.

idiosyncratic: Hyperscaler concentration: the company itself flags the customer concentration and supply considerations tied to AI infrastructure demand, which grew to approximately 6% of revenue and is expected to drive fiscal 2027. The risk factors note that demand from service providers and cloud customers fluctuates and that large orders can swing a quarter. A pause by a few buyers would hit both revenue and the order narrative. Monitor quarterly hyperscaler order figures against the fiscal 2027 revenue expectation.

Memory costs and margin: product gross margin fell on mix and higher memory costs, and the company describes memory constraints as part of a complex environment. Hardware-heavy AI revenue may carry lower margins than the rest of the mix. Monitor non-GAAP gross margin against the 65% - 66% Q1 fiscal 2027 range.

Inventory and commitments: inventories rose sharply in fiscal 2026, and the risk factors warn that procuring components to meet demand increases inventory and purchase commitments that may become excess if demand slows. Monitor inventory levels and the provision for inventory and purchase commitments.

Earnings quality and restructuring: GAAP EPS runs well below non-GAAP EPS, and the risk factors say changes in the business model could result in significant restructuring charges; Q4 fiscal 2026 restructuring and other charges rose to $511 million from $35 million. Repeated charges would keep the GAAP multiple elevated. Monitor restructuring charges and the GAAP to non-GAAP gap.

Refinancing and liquidity: short-term debt roughly doubled over the year and the current ratio sits below 1.0, so Cisco depends on rolling commercial paper and maturing notes. Interest coverage is comfortable today, but higher rates would raise interest cost. Monitor the mix of short-term debt and the use of cash for buybacks.
risks.systemic: The risk factors cite tariffs and other trade barriers, inflation, central bank policy uncertainty, and geopolitical instability including the Russia and Ukraine war, Middle East conflicts and China-Taiwan relations. These may reduce IT spending by service provider, cloud and enterprise customers, increase price competition, and create excess inventory or supply constraints. Cisco's exposure runs through enterprise and service-provider capital budgets and through its supply chain for components such as memory. An AI capital-spending slowdown across the industry would hit the hyperscaler business first, while a broad recession would hit enterprise and campus demand.

body: HOLD, 12-month target range $105 to $140. Cisco's fiscal 2026 shows real acceleration, broad order growth and disciplined operating expenses, but the growth is hardware-led and concentrated, margins and free cash flow moved the wrong way, and the stock already trades at 21.9x consensus FY27E EPS. Our weighted value is above the price but short of the BUY threshold, and the bear case is a credible downside.

We would move to BUY if non-GAAP gross margin finishes fiscal 2027 at or above the top of the 65% - 66% Q1 guided range while revenue tracks the upper half of the $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion guide, or if the price fell toward our Bear value without a change in the outlook. We would move to SELL if the company cut its fiscal 2027 hyperscaler AI revenue expectation below $7.5 billion or lowered its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance.
